newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr steady by Tokyo noon, large pound buying seen.
newsitem.headline: Dlr steady by Tokyo noon, large pound buying seen.

text.p: 0300 GMT TRADED HIGH/LOW AS OF 0300 GMT
The dollar was steady by Tokyo midday on Tuesday due to buy-back interest by overseas speculative funds and public and private institutional investors, traders said.
The buy-back came after Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka called recent forex movements excessive and said Japan will deal appropriately with excessive currency moves.
The dollar's recovery against the yen from early lows was also helped by a large quantity of sterling purchases for the yen by a major local brokerage firm.
"One of the Big Four (brokerages) tapped the pound/yen market with 300 million sterling worth of bids in early trading," said a chief trader at a long-term bank.

Sterling was quoted at about 184.30 yen when the big purchases happened. It stood at 184.50/60 yen at 0348 GMT, up from 184.14 yen at 2400 GMT. Traders said the large bids were partly related to recent launch of 200 million sterling three-year eurobond by Inter-American Development Bank.
